description:
FILED s464ax from the #985 probe battery (50 slice shapes vs perl 5.40.3).
PRE-EXISTING â reproduces on main `80b715c`; #985's change is emission- and
behaviour-identical on it.

    my %h = (a=>1);
    sub s1 { join(',', map { defined $_ ? $_ : 'U' } @_) }
    my $s = s1(@h{'a','zz'});
    print exists $h{zz} ? 1 : 0, "\n";     # perl 1, PCL 0

    my %h4 = (a=>1);
    for (@h4{'a','zz'}) { }
    print exists $h4{zz} ? 1 : 0, "\n";    # perl 1, PCL 0

The two spellings that do NOT vivify agree already:

    my @v = @h{'a','zz'};      # perl 0, PCL 0
    my @w = @h{'a','zz'};      # ditto in list-assign position

So the rule is perl's ordinary one â a hash slice is a list of LVALUES, and
taking an ALIAS to one (the @_ binding of a sub call, a foreach loop
variable) vivifies the element, while merely COPYING the values does not.
PCL's `p-hslice` already returns aliases (#818, `%p-alias-helem`), which is
why `for (@g{'p','q'}) { $_ .= '!' }` writes through; what it does not do is
CREATE the entry for a key that is absent, so the alias for a missing key is
an undef that goes nowhere.

WHERE TO LOOK: `%p-alias-helem` in cl/pcl-runtime.lisp and whatever
non-vivifying read it takes for an absent key.  Note the discriminator is not
the slice â it is whether the CONSUMER aliases, and PCL cannot see that from
inside p-hslice.  So the honest fix is probably the same shape as perl's:
p-hslice vivifies (a hash slice in rvalue context is `OPpLVAL_INTRO`-free but
perl's pp_hslice still creates the HE when the slice is an lvalue/alias
context)... which means the CONTEXT has to reach the runtime, or the
vivification has to happen in the alias-taking consumer.  MEASURE which
consumers exist before designing: @_ binding, foreach, `\(@h{...})`, list
assignment LHS.  Do not widen p-hslice unconditionally â `my @v = @h{'a','zz'}`
must keep NOT vivifying (probed).

SIZE: unknown; no baseline row is known to sit behind it (found by probe, not
by a failing test).  A filler.

=== DONE (s473b) ===
FIXED s473b (Opus, 2026-09-07), commit 2a6f0634.
THE RULE, measured before it was written (scratch/s473b/probe/m1010b.pl, 28
shapes vs perl 5.40.3): a slice vivifies its missing slots when the CONSUMER
ALIASES them â a sub-call or method-call argument (@_), a foreach, a map/grep
block ($_ aliases), `\(â¦)` â and creates nothing when the consumer COPIES
(list assignment, `()=`, join, sort, push, interpolation, `%h{â¦}`, scalar
context).  This task's guess that "map does NOT vivify" was WRONG: map and
grep alias $_, so they do.  A `($)` prototype does not change the answer
either, and perl vivifies EVERY key of the slice there, not just the one the
scalar read keeps.
ONE REWRITE RULE (`%p-aliasing-slice-form`, the twin of #1205's
`%p-copying-slice-form`), five consumers: p-foreach / p-foreach-raw (the
shared expander â and it reaches inside the emitter's
`(p-flatten-args (list â¦))` so a two-slice foreach cannot answer differently
from a one-slice one), compiler macros on p-map / p-grep / p-refgen-list, and
the emitter's `p-viv-slice` marker on a slice ARGUMENT of a user sub / method
/ coderef call (a called function cannot see its argument's form â the #1241
marker shape).  The vivifying readers `%p-aslice-viv` / `%p-hslice-viv` ask
the runtime's EAGER element accessors `p-aref-box` / `p-gethash-box`, so a
slice and a single element vivify by ONE piece of code.
The task's "widen p-hslice unconditionally" worry is answered by that split:
the default stays non-vivifying, so a consumer the rule misses keeps today's
read â the status quo, never a wrong value.
RESULT: 27 of 28 probe shapes identical (the base agreed on 21).  The residue
is `my $r; for (@$r{'a'})` â a deref-rooted slice whose ROOT has the raw-slot
verdict; PRE-EXISTING and NOT about aliasing (same answer on 782bc37e and in
the copying consumer; PCL_OPT=none gets it right) â filed as #1352.
BARS: gate green; corpus-diff 22/111 vs main, ALL MARKER-ONLY (this member adds
ZERO markers to perl-tests â no slice is a user-sub argument there â and one to
Pl/t/shapes/operand-grammar.pl); ir-host-leak 31 = base; artifacts regenerate
byte-identical; docs/ir-op-inventory.* regenerated with p-viv-slice in the
`elements` family; ir-spec Â§3.2d is the normative statement.
Guards: Pl/t/autoviv-02.t rows 14 (18 aliasing shapes) + 15 (10 copying
negatives), inverse-verified on the 782bc37e extraction â row 14 FAILS there,
row 15 PASSES, which is the point of having both.
subject: A hash slice's element ALIASED into @_ or a foreach does not vivify the missing key (perl does)
